segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹשִׁיב אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ חֶנְווֹנִית, אוֹ שֶׁמִּינָּהּ אַפּוֹטְרוֹפְּיָא — הֲרֵי זֶה מַשְׁבִּיעָהּ כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיִּרְצֶה. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ עַל פִּילְכָּהּ וְעַל עִיסָּתָהּ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If there is «one who establishes his wife» as a «storekeeper» in his store, «or» if «he appointed her» as a «steward» to handle his property and workers, «this» one, i.e., the husband, can «administer an oath to her,» having her state that she did not appropriate any of his possessions, «whenever he wants. Rabbi Eliezer says:» He can administer an oath «even with regard to» the products of «her spindle and for her dough,» which are matters related to the household, and not her function as a storekeeper.

moves.summary: A husband who makes his wife storekeeper or steward may have her swear whenever he wishes.
Even about her spindle and dough.
